ctx.s: {準備万端[じゅんびばんたん]}のつもりだったが、肝心[かんじん]のパスポートを家[いえ]に忘[わす]れていた。
ctx.en: I thought I was completely ready, but I had left the one thing that mattered, my passport, at home.

bad.s: 大掃除[おおそうじ]の日[ひ]、部屋[へや]の隅々[すみずみ]まで{準備万端[じゅんびばんたん]}に磨[みが]いた。
bad.en: (meant: on cleaning day I polished every corner of the room thoroughly)
bad.why: It says preparations are complete and you are ready; it is not an adverb for doing a job thoroughly. Say tetteiteki ni migaita.

bad.s: まだ何[なに]もしていないから、そろそろ{準備万端[じゅんびばんたん]}を始[はじ]めよう。
bad.en: (meant: I haven't done anything yet, so let's start getting ready)
bad.why: It means the preparations are already finished, so it cannot be something you start. Say junbi o hajimeyou.

mean: excelling at both studies and sport
lit: both paths: the way of letters and the way of arms, once the ideal of the samurai

use.how: Xは文武両道だ / 文武両道の生徒 / 文武両道を掲げる: praise for someone, usually a student, who is strong in both schoolwork and sport.

near.diff: 才色兼備 praises a woman for both talent and beauty; 文武両道 praises anyone for both studies and sport.

cue: The captain of the school football team also comes top of the year in every exam. How do teachers sum her up?

ctx.s: 兄[あに]は勉強[べんきょう]もスポーツもできる{文武両道[ぶんぶりょうどう]}だ。
ctx.en: My brother is good at both his studies and sport.

ctx.s: うちの高校[こうこう]は{文武両道[ぶんぶりょうどう]}を掲[かか]げている。
ctx.en: My high school's motto is excellence in both studies and sport.

ctx.s: 「野球部[やきゅうぶ]のキャプテンで、成績[せいせき]も学年[がくねん]トップなんだって。」「まさに{文武両道[ぶんぶりょうどう]}だね。」
ctx.en: "He's captain of the baseball team and top of his year too." "A true all-rounder, then."

ctx.s: 彼女[かのじょ]は部活[ぶかつ]と受験勉強[じゅけんべんきょう]を両立[りょうりつ]させ、三年間[さんねんかん]{文武両道[ぶんぶりょうどう]}を貫[つらぬ]いた。
ctx.en: She balanced club activities with exam study and kept up both for all three years.

ctx.s: 江戸時代[えどじだい]の武士[ぶし]には、学問[がくもん]と武芸[ぶげい]の{文武両道[ぶんぶりょうどう]}が求[もと]められた。
ctx.en: Samurai in the Edo period were expected to master both learning and the martial arts.

ctx.s: 医師[いし]として働[はたら]きながらマラソン選手[せんしゅ]としても活躍[かつやく]する彼[かれ]は、{文武両道[ぶんぶりょうどう]}の人[ひと]だ。
ctx.en: He works as a doctor and competes as a marathon runner: a man of both brains and brawn.

bad.s: 彼[かれ]は数学[すうがく]も英語[えいご]も得意[とくい]な{文武両道[ぶんぶりょうどう]}だ。
bad.en: (meant: he is good at both maths and English)
bad.why: Maths and English are both studies; the idiom needs sport or physical skill as the other half. Just say suugaku mo eigo mo tokui da.

bad.s: 彼女[かのじょ]は頭[あたま]がよくて美人[びじん]で、まさに{文武両道[ぶんぶりょうどう]}だ。
bad.en: (meant: she is clever and beautiful)
bad.why: Beauty is not sport. For talent together with looks, the idiom is saishoku kenbi.
